newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean bankers summoned over Hanbo loan scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean bankers summoned over Hanbo loan scandal.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors said they were questioning heads of two leading local banks and a former president of a state bank on Tuesday over a loan scandal surrounding insolvent Hanbo Steel Co.
"The three were summoned today and are now being questioned at the prosecution office," senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog told reporters.
They are Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank, Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung Bank and Lee Hyung-koo, former chief of the state-run Korea Development Bank.
Prosecution officials said the bankers would be questioned on whether they received commissions in return for offering huge loans to Hanbo Steel, the country's second largest steelmaker.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group, the 14th largest conglomerate in South Korea, piled up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
President Kim Young-sam, who ordered a thorough probe into the loans last week, has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
Finance Ministry officials said Korea First, Cho Hung and Korea Development were Hanbo Steel's three main creditor banks, with combined outstanding loans of 2.4 trillion won.
Prosecutors arrested Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo last Friday on charges of fraud and violating laws on cheques and trust and savings companies.

The prosecutors had also questioned other officials of Hanbo and creditor banks over a lobbying fund kept by Chung and examined Hanbo's bank accounts to find out if there were irregularities, Choi said.
At a weekend meeting with top aides at the presidential Blue House, President Kim expressed frustration over an anti-graft campaign he launched when he took office in 1993.
Kim's popularity, which topped 90 percent when he kicked off the anti-corruption drive, has plunged and is now near single digits according to some recent surveys.
His image has been hurt in the past year by the resignation of several top officials, including a defence minister, who have been charged with taking bribes.
